➡️ Hong Kong man loses HK$13 million in fake crypto investment app scam 

🌐 A Hong Kong man in his 70s has lost more than HK$13 million ($1.67 million) after a self-described cryptocurrency investment expert contacted him through WhatsApp and directed him to a fake trading app. The latest case began when the elderly man received an unsolicited WhatsApp message from someone claiming to be a cryptocurrency investment expert from Singapore. The person introduced him to what was presented as a crypto platform offering favorable exchange rates, low fees and withdrawals at any time.

‼️ Following the instructions he received, the man opened a cryptocurrency wallet and purchased Tether (USDT) and Ethereum (ETH). He was then told to download an investment application supplied by the scammer and transfer the cryptocurrency to designated wallet addresses as investment capital.

📣 Seeing his account balance rise inside the app, the victim became less suspicious and continued sending more cryptocurrency to the wallets provided by the scammer. The fraud only became clear when he tried to withdraw his funds and was repeatedly prevented from doing so under different pretexts. By the time the victim realized the investment platform was fraudulent, his losses had exceeded HK$13 million.

💬 Pezeshkian calls for deeper Iran-Azerbaijan ties, implementation of agreements

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for stronger ties with Azerbaijan, stressing that shared borders should not become an obstacle to expanding relations and urging faster development of road, air and rail links between the two neighbors.

President Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday, during a meeting with Azeri Deputy Prime Minister Shahin Mustafayev, who was in Tehran for talks with Iranian officials.
​
The Iranian president said Azerbaijan holds a special place in Iran's neighborhood policy and described the two nations as relatives and brothers. He called for maximum use of their capacities and geographic advantages to deepen bilateral relations and strengthen people-to-people ties.
​
President Pezeshkian noted that the two countries' scientific, cultural, economic, political and security relations are closely interconnected, saying joint efforts were needed to further consolidate cooperation.
​
He emphasized that the common border should be used as an opportunity to expand interaction rather than becoming a barrier to closer relations. He also welcomed understandings reached during Mustafayev's meetings with Iran's ministers of roads and urban development and energy, calling for their rapid implementation.
​
The president also described transportation and communications networks as key tools for connecting the two countries and their peoples. He said land, air and rail routes should be expanded and better integrated, arguing that stronger connectivity would create greater opportunities to consolidate bilateral relations.
​
President Pezeshkian called for continued joint efforts to implement agreements and advance the mutual interests of both nations.
​
Mustafayev, for his part, briefed the Iranian president on his discussions with several ministers in Tehran and the understandings reached during those talks.
​
The Azerbaijani official reaffirmed Baku's determination to further develop relations with Tehran and stressed the need to follow up on and implement existing agreements and understandings.
​
He also highlighted the commitment of Tehran and Baku to expanding transport and communications cooperation, emphasizing the importance of strengthening transit routes and corridors and making greater use of existing capacities in this area.

🥇 Gold Purchases Might Be Higher Than Reported

Central banks around the world bought 44 tonnes of gold in July—up 158% compared to the pre-2022 average of 17 tonnes, according to Goldman Sachs.

The 3-month average now stands at 91 tonnes, nearing its highest level since mid-2025. Meanwhile, the 12-month moving average has remained steady between 50 and 60 tonnes in recent months.

Official data, however, only recorded 23 tonnes purchased in July—21 tonnes short of the actual figure. Monthly official purchases haven’t exceeded 60 tonnes since November 2024, indicating that central bank demand for gold could be significantly underreported.
